body:
## Problem

List endpoints return HTTP 500 when `page` is close to `math.MaxInt`. With an admin JWT on a local instance built from `main` (dba770d56):

```
GET /api/v1/admin/users?page=9223372036854775807
{"code":500,"message":"internal error"}
```

The server log shows `pq: OFFSET must not be negative`. `page=461168601842738791` still returns 200, because `(page-1)*20` just fits in int64 there.

On the same instance, 12 list requests with `page=9223372036854775807` returned 500:

| Endpoint | Failure |
|---|---|
| `/api/v1/admin/users`, `/api/v1/usage`, `/api/v1/keys`, `/api/v1/admin/payment/orders` | `OFFSET must not be negative` |
| `/api/v1/admin/affiliates/users`, `/api/v1/admin/audit-logs`, `/api/v1/admin/channels`, `/api/v1/admin/ops/system-logs` | `OFFSET must not be negative` |
| `/api/v1/admin/prompt-audit/events`, `/api/v1/admin/ops/dashboard/openai-token-stats` | `OFFSET must not be negative` |
| `/api/v1/admin/groups?sort_by=account_count`, `/api/v1/admin/users/:id/balance-history` | panic `slice bounds out of range [:-20]`, turned into 500 by the recovery middleware |

## Root cause

- `PaginationParams.Offset()` (`internal/pkg/pagination/pagination.go`) only normalizes `Page < 1` and then computes `(Page-1)*Limit()` with no overflow guard.
- `response.ParsePagination` accepts any positive page, so `(page-1)*pageSize` wraps around. An even page size gives a negative offset, which PostgreSQL rejects; in-memory pagination (`paginateSlice`, `mergeBalanceHistoryCodes`) panics on the negative slice bound. An odd page size wraps to a large positive offset and silently returns an empty page.
- Several repositories compute `(page-1)*pageSize` themselves, so fixing `Offset()` alone does not cover them. The prompt audit event list and the OpenAI token stats filter parse `page` on their own with no upper bound.

## Fix

- `Offset()` keeps the `Page < 1` → 1 rule and the 1..1000 limit, then saturates `Page` at `math.MaxInt/limit`. Both `offset` and `offset+limit` then fit in `int`, which the in-memory paths need.
- `ParsePagination` clamps `page` the same way after reading the page size. Every caller that multiplies on its own gets a safe page, so the repositories stay untouched. A clamped request returns an empty page, the same as any page past the end, and the response's `page` field echoes the clamped value (for example `461168601842738790` at page size 20).
- The prompt audit event list and the OpenAI token stats filter already answer invalid pagination with 400; an overflowing page now gets that same 400. This mirrors the existing guard in `GET /api/v1/redeem/history`.

## Tests

New cases in the existing tables:

- `TestPaginationParamsOffsetUsesNormalizedLimit`: `page=MaxInt` with page sizes 20, 21 (odd) and 1000, the exact saturation bound, and one past it.
- `TestPaginationParamsOffsetDoesNotOverflow` (new): for large pages × page sizes {1, 2, 3, 20, 21, 999, 1000}, `0 <= offset <= MaxInt-limit`, and repeated calls return the same value.
- `TestParsePagination`: `page=9223372036854775807` (with default and 1000 page size), the exact bound `461168601842738790`, and one past it.
- `TestParseOpsOpenAITokenStatsFilter_InvalidParams` and `TestPromptAdminRejectsInvalidEventIDsTimesAndPagination`: `page=9223372036854775807` is rejected.

The new cases fail on `main` and pass with this change.

```
$ cd backend
$ go test -tags=unit -count=1 ./internal/pkg/pagination/ ./internal/pkg/response/ ./internal/securityaudit/ ./internal/handler/admin/
ok  	github.com/Wei-Shaw/sub2api/internal/pkg/pagination	0.005s
ok  	github.com/Wei-Shaw/sub2api/internal/pkg/response	0.007s
ok  	github.com/Wei-Shaw/sub2api/internal/securityaudit	0.027s
ok  	github.com/Wei-Shaw/sub2api/internal/handler/admin	0.024s

$ go test -tags=unit -count=1 ./...
58 packages ok, 0 failures

$ golangci-lint run ./internal/pkg/pagination/... ./internal/pkg/response/... ./internal/securityaudit/... ./internal/handler/admin/...   # v2.14.0, as in CI
0 issues.
```

Manual check on the same local instance with the patched binary: every request in the table above, plus `/api/v1/admin/proxies?sort_by=account_count`, `/api/v1/keys?sort_by=current_concurrency` and `/api/v1/usage?page_size=21`, returns 200 with an empty page, except prompt-audit events and openai-token-stats, which return 400. The server log has no `OFFSET must not be negative` and no panic.
title: fix(pagination): keep page offsets from overflowing int
